For when he rose, all came out ahead to meet him with dances and songs and tambourines, saying to one another, "Come, let us rejoice in the Lord; let us shout aloud to the God of Jacob." Others danced and said, "He ascended on high, he led captivity captive, he gave gifts among men." Some even called everyone to come and look, saying, "Shout to God, all the earth; sing now to his name," and again, "Come and see the works of the Lord: terrible in his counsels above the sons of men, making wars cease to the end of the earth." For there is no longer enmity and war; everything is at peace, since the enemy lies dead and the one who once played the tyrant is bound hand and foot. Others again, who knew the devil's insolence and his great ambushes, and now saw him dead, said in amazement, "How has the morning star fallen from heaven, he who rose at dawn?" and, "How has the hammer of the whole earth been broken and shattered?" For along with wonder, perplexity gripped them all. They marveled to see the great tyrant suddenly lying dead like this, but they were at a loss as to the cause of his fall, above all because they did not believe that death could be abolished by a death, or that so great a serpent could be dashed down on a cross. So again they marveled and said, "How has Babylon been taken?" For now they saw that Hades too had been plundered. 28. Seeing these things and hearing them, the wretch raged and wasted away in lamentation. For indeed [?]

"...and he will gnash his teeth at him. But the Lord will laugh him to scorn," and again, "The sinner will see and be angry; he will gnash his teeth and melt away." He gnashed his teeth in regret that he had ever dared to move against the Savior at all, knowing that before this he had dared to move against the righteous and suffered nothing of the kind. For when he plotted against Abel, oppressed the patriarchs, plotted against Isaiah too, insulted Jeremiah and tempted Job, he still kept his strength, and death reigned from Adam to Moses. But now that he has dared to move against the Lord, he sees that he has become a beggar like Irus, cast out of everything and trampled by everyone. For the Savior's work was not only to make a mockery of death itself, but also to set us upon it, so that he might not only free us from slavery but also bring to nothing the one who enslaved us, lest he grow strong again, deceive us, and make the Savior's achievement come to nothing. So, having made a mockery of death, he now hands it over to us as well to be trampled on, saying, "Behold, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy," and again, "He will trample lion and dragon." Long ago the serpent deceived Eve, and through his envy death came into the world; but now he is trampled underfoot, and when he tries to deceive he hears, "Get behind me, Satan." Long ago our adversary the devil prowled like a lion, thirsting for our soul; but now he is trampled underfoot together with the dragon, and soon God will crush Satan under our feet. He is so despised and mocked that a person can put his hand into an asp's hole without fear. For Isaiah prophesied this, and the saying is [?]

29. Children, at any rate, now laugh at the pleasure that once deceived even old men; before they have even reached the age of the law they gird themselves with a chastity that goes beyond the law. Remaining virgins, they trample by the Word on the deceits of serpent-like pleasure, unafraid of its deadly bites. Some have even trampled on the devil's sting itself and did not shrink from death; rather they exchanged their life for death, becoming martyrs of the Word. For this is why the Lord died. Many, having left behind the things of earth, pass through the air with free step and live as citizens of heaven, no longer afraid of the ruler of the air; instead they rebuke him, and if he tries to hinder them they say, "Get behind me, Satan, for I am hastening to worship the Lord my God." For this is why the Savior was crucified in the air. And the way to paradise, which long ago

was shut through sin, now stands open to all who wish, as Paul testifies, who was caught up there and went into the heavens. For this is why the Lord made sport of the serpent. Hades has been abolished: death no longer holds sway, but all are raised up. The devil no longer rises against us, for he has fallen, and having truly fallen, he goes on his breast and belly. For this is why the Lord rose. Human beings have learned to despise bodily wealth and are rich in the Word and in knowledge, while the dragon who boasted of being rich has been stripped bare and is now a naked Irus, a pauper, plundered by all. For long ago he dwelt in the midst of the cherubim, clothed in every precious stone, sardius, jasper and agate; but now he sleeps among papyrus and reed and pebbles, as is said of him in Job. For this is why the Lord became poor: that we might become rich through his poverty, and that the devil might be stripped bare. And a strange and great thing has come about in creation: human beings hasten to die, praying for the Savior's coming, while the wretched devil, who once held the power of death, now fears the one who is coming and cowers before the judgment. For he knows the fire prepared for him and his angels. For this is why my Lord was judged: to free us from judgment and to condemn him. 30. As for the knowledge of God that has come to all people everywhere, what need is there even to speak of it, when the events themselves carry their own proof? Not a day passes in which people do not abandon idols, renounce their own ancestral laws, take refuge with God, and ask to receive the laws of Christ, believing in him through a marvelous wonder. For while still worshiping idols and slandering Christ as a mere man, they later come to know him as God and abandon the idols; the demons they used to fear in the idols, once they have come to know the Lord, they now forsake, and even drive them out of others; the pleasure they feared [?] as idolaters they despise in Christ; and the sin that once overcame them they now overcome by the sign of the cross and make sport of it. For though they once utterly disbelieved in virginity, saying it was impossible for this virtue to be found among human beings, once they have believed in the Savior born of a virgin they not only acknowledge it but live by it themselves, and are disbelieved by those who are still pagan idolaters. Besides this, all sorcery has ceased, all magic has been abolished, and all the wisdom of the Greeks has been made foolish. For in divine matters what is needed is not words but deeds, and what helps is not the utterance of the tongue but the disposition of the soul. So the Greeks cannot grasp by words what Christians demonstrate by faith; and what the magicians bring about by words, that, even while we

keep silent, is abolished by the sign of the cross. What they doubt about immortality, the martyrs of Christ demonstrate not by words but by deeds. The virginity that the magicians and the philosophers of the Greeks call into question, even women display in Christ. The demons they pray to as gods, even children in Christ drive out. In short, the man who bears Christ is like a god on earth: he is forbearing toward men, and to all he displays the heavenly life, as though he went about with the sun. 31. See, this is a single achievement of the cross; see, this is what the Savior's death has done. For the work is not a man's but God's. That is why he suffered as a man: to grant to human beings things that are above humanity and divine. So the achievements now seen among human beings are his. For even if Paul speaks, it is Christ who speaks in him; even if he does great and wonderful things, it is the grace of Christ that accomplishes them; and though the knowledge of God has reached everyone, the teaching is not of men but of the Word himself, who came down as mediator between God and men. For this is written, which the Jews once passed over in silence but now see fulfilled; for it is written, "They shall all be taught by God," just as Jeremiah also says, "Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord," and goes on to say, "And each will not teach his neighbor, and each his brother, saying, 'Know the Lord,' for all will know me, from the least of them to the greatest, for I will be merciful to their iniquities." For who is it that pricks the hearts of people among their idols, if not the Lord? And who draws them out from there while they are still serving idols, if not Christ himself, who says, "When I am lifted up, I will draw all to myself"? For the wonder is this: while they are still serving idols, the mind of their soul is opened so that they understand that those they once thought to be gods are wood and stone, and recognize that the one they mocked as crucified is not a man but God. And the teacher of the mind is not a man, but God, who alone sees the mind. Truly blessed and life-giving cross of the Savior! You triumphed over death and destroyed the devil who held it. Divine Word, and truly the Wisdom of the Father! You uncovered the face of the crafty one and laid bare the fold of his breastplate, so that we too can say, "For we are not ignorant of his designs." Loving and good Master! You redeemed us when we were captives, and when we were slaves to sin, Lord, you set us free through your own death. For we know that we have been freed from sin. Truly the peacemaker, Son of God! You restored to us our adoption as sons, and having reconciled

us to your own Father, you abolished the enmity in your flesh. Rich Savior and true King! For you became poor, so that by your poverty we might become rich; you also granted us the kingdom of heaven, Creator and Maker of all things, Word of the Father! For you created us anew, and we are your workmanship, created for good works. Truly Light and radiance of the Father! For you shone upon us in darkness, and led us, who could not see, into the light. Truly Form and Image of the Father! For you formed us anew when we were perishing, and granted us again what is according to the image. God the Word and truly Life! For you gave life to us when we had died, and renewed us when we had been corrupted, clothing us with incorruption. Truly Power, and Arm, and Right Hand of the Father! For you loosed the pangs of death and shattered the bronze doors and iron bars, as Scripture says. You also led the dragon, the serpent, the devil, around on a human hook in the trophy of the cross. Because of you and your divine valor, all trample on him and all make a mockery of him. For since you were the first to make sport of him, it has now come true that he is "the beginning of the Lord's creation, made to be mocked." And since you cast him down, he has become a wonder to all, so that they say, "How has the morning star fallen from heaven, he who rose at dawn?" And since you took from him the bond that stood against us and nailed it to the cross, all jeer at him, saying, "How the exactor has ceased! The taskmaster has ceased! God has broken the yoke of sinners. For now decay is spread beneath him, and the worm is his covering." And no one fears the dragon any longer; instead they worship you, and through you the Father. 32. Thus, then, the Lord rose up and swiftly made a mockery of death, and freed us from it. But the Jews were not ashamed even when they saw these things; rather, in daring to move against the Savior they did not realize that they were undertaking all this against themselves. For in handing over the Lord they did not see that they were calling down the handing over of Jerusalem, as the prophet Jeremiah says: "Jerusalem shall surely be handed over into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon." Nor did they see that, by refusing to serve the Lord, they were making themselves slaves to the devil and serving him in the plot against the Savior. For in asking for Barabbas and killing the Lord, they did not know that they would live the life of Barabbas, that every kind of sedition and murder would grow among them, and that they would cast away from themselves the light and the truth and all that the Lord is, as Isaiah says: "Behold now, the Master, the Lord of hosts, will take away from Judea and from Jerusalem the strong man and the strong woman, the strength of bread and the strength of water, the giant

and the strong man, the warrior and the judge, the prophet and the diviner, the elder and the captain of fifty, the wonderful counselor, the wise master builder and the intelligent listener. And I will set young men as their rulers, and mockers shall lord it over them." For the wretches mocked the Lord and did not see that the prophetic word was being fulfilled against them, which says, "Mockers shall lord it over them." For this is the wonder of the Savior: when he was crucified, he suffered on behalf of humanity, yet made a mockery of death, while what was written was fulfilled against the Jews. That the light too has been taken from them is written in Jeremiah thus: "The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah." Then he goes on to say, "I will take away from them the voice of gladness and the voice of joy, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the scent of perfume and the light of the lamp." Indeed, they handed the Lord over to the Gentiles and did not know, but were blind to the fact, that before long they themselves would be defiled among the Gentiles, and the Gentiles would come against them into their inheritance, as it is written: "O God, the nations have come into your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem a watchman's hut in an orchard." In refusing to have the Lord as king, they did not know that they were being stripped of the honor of David. For the kingdom of David was laid up for him, and it lasted until the Savior's appearing, as Jacob testifies when he says, "A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his loins, until there comes the one for whom it is laid up, and he is the expectation of the nations." And when they stripped the Lord and beat him, they did not know that they were being stripped by him and were provoking lamentation against themselves. For the Lord himself says, "I will take away my garments and my linen, so that they do not cover her shame," and again, "Therefore she will beat her breast and lament; she will go barefoot and naked; she will make lamentation like dragons and mourning like daughters of sirens." And when they had a scarlet cloak thrown over him, they did not see that they were fulfilling against themselves the Spirit's accusation, "Your hands are full of blood." And as they rejoiced at the crown of thorns set around the Savior, they were blind to the fact that they were placing the thorns around themselves. For it is written: "Be amazed, be grieved, you who are confident; strip, make yourselves naked, gird your loins, and beat your breasts for the field of your desire and for the fruit of the vine. Thorns and grass will spring up on the land of my people, and gladness will be taken away from every house." They mocked

the Lord as the Son of God, and did not see that they were casting away their own adoption as sons, as he himself testifies, saying, "I begot sons and raised them up, but they rejected me," and, "Behold, your house is left to you." They gave him vinegar and gall to drink, but this too was utterly blind and against themselves. For God brought a vine out of Egypt and planted it, and waited to receive fruit from it, grapes and wine; but the fools gave him vinegar instead of wine and gall instead of grapes, revealing the mark of their Sodom-like wickedness, for their grape is gall, as is written in Deuteronomy. This is why our Lord and Savior, knowing the kind of fruit they would bear, told them beforehand the parable of the vineyard, and that the kingdom of heaven would be taken away from you and given to a nation that produces its fruits. Besides this, they divided his garments among the executioners, not seeing the dividing that would be done against them among the Gentiles. For the prophet says: "Behold, the days of the Lord are coming, and your spoils will be divided in your midst. And I will gather all the nations to war against Jerusalem, and the city will be taken, the houses plundered, and the women defiled," and again, "Now the blight will devour their portions," and as Micah says: "On that day a parable will be taken up against you, and a lament will be sung with a tune, saying, 'The portion of my people has been utterly ruined; it has been measured out with a line; there was no one to stop it from being turned away; your fields have been parceled out.'" In short, by daring to move against the Lord, they called down upon themselves the day that the prophet also foretold: "For it is the day of the Lord's judgment, the year of recompense for the judgment of Zion. Her ravines will be turned into pitch, and her soil into sulfur. Her land will be like pitch burning night and day, and it will not be quenched for all time, and its smoke will go up on high. It will be laid waste for generations, and birds and hedgehogs, ibises and ravens will dwell in it. The measuring line of a wilderness will be cast over it, and donkey-centaurs will live in it. Her rulers will be no more, and her kings and her great men will go to destruction. And there will spring up in her [?]... And it will be a haunt of sirens and a court of ostriches, and demons will meet with donkey-centaurs, and they will cry out to one another. There the donkey-centaurs will rest, for they have found a resting place for themselves. There the hedgehog has made its nest, and the earth has kept its plains safe." 33. These things the Jews suffered, thinking that they were killing the Lord; these things they called down upon themselves by crying out against the Savior; in these things [?]

…were judged, having wished to judge the Lord. Let anyone who wishes come forward and be judge, reckoning the truth not from hidden matters but from what has actually happened. Let him consider what fruit the Lord's death bore, and what the Jews gained by their plot. The Saviour's death set the world free, and the nations glorified God; but the rage of the Jews destroyed their city along with the Jews themselves, and blinded them to the knowledge of God. The Lord's death brought the dead to life; but the plot of the Jews robbed the Jews themselves of life, and now they are without the Lord. The Saviour's cross filled the Church of the nations, which had been desolate; but the Jews by their own wickedness made themselves desolate even of the world, and now they have no city. Again, the Saviour's death revealed the kingdom of heaven; but the Jews in their rage destroyed even their own kings and brought down their great men. Besides this, the Lord's cross joined angels to human beings and became the mediator of their friendship; but the Jews by their plotting gained a dwelling with demons. Christ's death relieved the brutishness into which humanity had fallen through sin; but the Jews became brutish through their rage, and now in their ways they keep company with sirens and hedgehogs and ostriches, having a character as monstrous as onocentaurs. For among them lawlessness has taken the place of the law, and in place of gentleness they have rage, like that of the serpent. In short, there is nothing among them that does not work death for them. Is it not right, then, to cleave to that death and to forsake the council of the Pharisees? Is it not right rather to worship the cross than to win the friendship of the Jews and of the world? This is why the blessed Paul wrote, "I have counted all things loss, that I may gain Christ"; this is why he regards the cross as his boast, saying, "But far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world." This is why the Lord himself said, "Whoever does not take up his cross and follow me is not worthy of me, nor can he be my disciple."

34. But here great caution is needed, lest we take up the cross after the manner of the Jews and not after the manner of Paul. Paul bore the cross as a trophy of victory over sin; the Jews bore it in order to kill the Lord. That is why we must be on our guard and stay sober, lest, while accusing the Jews, we do the same things against the Lord as they did. For many who worship the Lord and [36: "of the dead." Regius, in a second hand: "without the … dead." The editions: "without the Lord."]

yet live unworthily of him do not realize that they are making themselves guilty of the Saviour's death. "For whoever eats the bread and drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily is guilty of the body and blood of the Lord," as the Apostle testifies. So too, "whoever hates his brother does not love the Lord," but hates him just as the Jews did. Whoever despises the poor man himself dishonours the Lord, as the Jews did; this is what Solomon says: "Whoever despises the poor dishonours the one who made him." Whoever overlooks a poor man who is hungry and thirsty and naked is like the Jews, who stripped the Lord and gave him vinegar and gall to drink. Whoever takes bribes against the innocent is no different from the one who sold the Lord, Judas; for he too sells justice, which is the Lord, as Judas sold Christ. Whoever does not judge on behalf of the orphan and render justice to the widow is the same as those who plotted against the Lord and slandered him. In a word, whatever anyone does to his neighbour is reckoned as done to the Lord, who came down for our sake and died on our behalf. For so the Lord says in the Gospels: "Inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me." And again—something it is necessary to know and to keep—"The fornicator destroys his own soul, and he too, like the Jews, outrages the temple and body of the Lord." For "whoever destroys the temple of God will be destroyed by God," as Paul writes. And whoever is ruled by sin falls in no way short of the Jews who denied the Lord and said they had no king but Caesar. Let the one who is mastered by pleasures, and who delights in them all the more, not be unaware that he too, like the Jews, asks for Barabbas and kills the Lord. For in just this way the Jews, having come to love the depraved character of Barabbas, drove virtue away. And let the one who is not strong in faith know that he is like those who disbelieved and said, "If he is the Son of God, let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in him." For they too spoke these words in unbelief. What, then, must we do in the face of all this? Nothing else than to believe in Christ and to live according to him, as Paul too says: "Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ"; to turn away from the friendship of the Jews, from their unbelief and mockery, and from "myths and endless genealogies, which promote speculations rather than God's plan, which is by faith"; and to hold fast to the cross, to live worthily of it, and to say the same words as Paul: "But far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ." For if we live in this way and

believe in the Lord, we shall come to know his ascension into heaven and his session at the right hand of the Majesty; we shall see the [?] of the angels, and his coming again in glory—which the angels announce beforehand and the saints celebrate in hymns, and all who behold it exult and rejoice in Christ Jesus, through whom be glory and power to the Father for ever and ever. Amen.

Athanasius, On the Passion. "Death reigned from Adam to Moses." But now, having dared to attack the Lord, it sees itself cast out of the universe, trampled by all, and crushed beneath our feet. What is great and astonishing is that even while the Lord hung upon the cross (for the body was his, and the Word was in it), the sun was darkened, the earth quaked, the rocks were split, the veil of the temple was torn, and many bodies of those who had fallen asleep were raised. And no one, as the Arians now dare to do, debated whether one ought to obey the Word made flesh. Rather, though they saw a man, they recognized him as their Creator; and though they heard a human voice, they did not say that the Word is a creature because of what was human. On the contrary, they trembled all the more, and recognized no less that he was speaking from a holy temple. For creation does not worship a creature; nor again did it refuse, because of the flesh, to worship its own Lord, but it saw its own Creator in the body. And at the name of Jesus Christ every knee bent and will bend, and every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord. For the flesh brought no dishonour on the Word—far from it!—rather, it was itself glorified by him. Nor, because the Son, who was in the form of God, took the form of a servant, was he diminished in his Godhead; rather, he became the liberator of all flesh and of all creation. Even while he was being crucified he was attested as Master of creation: the sun drew in its rays, the earth trembled, the rocks were split, and the executioners recognized that the one crucified was truly the Son of God. For the body that was seen was not that of some man, but of God; and being in it, even while he was being crucified, he raised the dead. Then the sun too, indignant and unable to bear the bodily outrages committed against the common Master of all—outrages he willingly endured for our sake—turned away, and, drawing in its rays, made that day sunless.
